display.title: Shabbos Candles: Melech HaOlam, Hashem Is King of the Whole World
display.summary_short: Mitzvah time on the Shabbos candle brachah: what 'Melech HaOlam' means, and how Hashem is the King of every country and the King of all kings.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, continuing a series on Neshek, the lighting of Shabbos candles. After reviewing last week's words, 'Baruch Atah, Hashem Elokeinu', Uncle Yossi teaches the next two words of the brachah: 'Melech HaOlam'. He describes what a king once was: people honored and feared him, because he could make the poor rich, imprison or free, and decide over life and death. Hashem is far greater than any king, for He is King of the whole world, every country, with full control of everything. That is what makes 'Atah', You, so special: in a brachah we speak directly to the King of the world. He connects this to Shalom Aleichem on Friday night, where Hashem is called the King of all kings, the Holy One, blessed be He. The lesson ends with a review of the first six words of the brachah.
display.lesson: When we make a brachah we are speaking directly to Hashem, the King of the whole world.
